context.objective: Document how we carry out Digital Binder Maintenance, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: To begin with, we set up the quarterly binder structure. That is done by fund accountant preparer. What we do: create the binder for the correct fund and quarter, or roll forward the prior binder by copying and updating it. Confirm the A, E, F, H, J, K, L, M, N, O, and Q categories are available. Allow access only to authorized users under the existing repository controls. The check on it: confirm the fund, entity, and period before filing if something is wrong. The exact creation process, file naming rules, permissions, and
Please finish what you were saying about the creation process, file naming rules, and permissions?

Next, we collect support before posting affected entries. That is done by process preparer fund accountant. What we do: identify the source documents and approvals that support the JE, confirm the documents match the entity, period, amount, and transaction, file the support before posting any JE affecting cost, income, expense, or capital. If the originating process provides a reference field, use it to link the posted entry to the filed support. The check on it: filing support before posting is the main required check if something is wrong. No documented emergency exception exists. Stop and escalate to.
Who is the issue escalated to when support is missing before posting?

After that, we classify records using the standard binder categories, that is done by fund accountant preparer. What we do: select the binder category that matches the supported balance or activity, use F for investments, E for cash, L for LOC, M for partners capital, N for contributions, O for distributions, Q for management fees, and the other defined categories as applicable. If one item supports multiple categories, keep one controlled copy and use an approved cross-reference if the repository supports it. The cross-reference method still needs confirmation. The check on it: supporting records must be easy to find from the related account or activity.
How do you check that a supporting record is easy to find from the related account or activity?

Then, we file close check and review records. That is done by fund accountant preparer. What we do: file the quarterly check of checks and the records showing how related exceptions were resolved. File marked tie-out PDFs, copies showing the comparison, under the applicable financial statement category: file cash, investment, accrual, capital, contribution, distribution, management fee, DTM, and LOC records under their categories. Keep review comments and approvals with the related support when the originating process requires them. The check on it. Keep internal review marks within GPFS if something is wrong, if an originating process has not produced a required record, log an.

steps.title: Set up quarterly binder
steps.description: Create a binder for the correct fund and quarter, or copy and update the prior binder.

steps.title: Confirm binder categories
steps.description: Confirm that categories A, E, F, H, J, K, L, M, N, O and Q are available.

steps.title: Restrict binder access
steps.description: Allow access only to authorized users under existing repository controls. How permissions are applied is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Confirm filing details
steps.description: Confirm the fund, entity and period before filing. The participant's wording about something being wrong needs clarification.

steps.title: Identify journal entry support
steps.description: Identify the source documents and approvals supporting the journal entry.

steps.title: Check support against entry
steps.description: Confirm the documents match the entity, period, amount and transaction.

steps.title: File journal entry support
steps.description: File support before posting any journal entry affecting cost, income, expense or capital.

steps.title: Post affected journal entry
steps.description: Post the affected entry after support is filed. If the originating process provides a reference field, use it to link the posted entry to the filed support; the precise timing and performer of the link are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Stop and escalate issue
steps.description: Stop and escalate if something is wrong. The escalation recipient and subsequent handling are UNKNOWN; no documented emergency exception exists.

steps.title: Classify supporting records
steps.description: Select the category matching the supported balance or activity: F for investments, E for cash, L for LOC, M for partners capital, N for contributions, O for distributions and Q for management fees. Use other defined categories as applicable and check that records are easy to find from the related account or activity.

steps.title: Handle multi-category support
steps.description: For an item supporting multiple categories, keep one controlled copy. Use an approved cross-reference if the repository supports it; the cross-reference method needs confirmation.

steps.title: File close and review records
steps.description: File the quarterly check of checks and records of related exception resolution. File marked tie-out PDFs and comparison copies under the applicable financial statement categories. Keep review comments and approvals with related support when the originating process requires them; keep internal review marks within GPFS.

steps.title: Log when record is missing
steps.description: If an originating process has not produced a required record, the participant says to log something but the statement ends before identifying what to log.
